output.title: Control board assembly on pallet carriers

product.name: Control board (PCB)
product.description: Small PCB assembled on a pallet carrier: 160 × 100 mm, 1.6 mm thick. The finished item is the populated board after reflow and optical inspection.

steps.name: ApplySolderPaste
steps.does: Dispense solder paste onto the PCB pads on the board mounted to the carrier.

steps.name: PlaceComponents
steps.does: A SCARA robot places about 20 components onto the pasted pads using parts from feeders.

steps.name: ReflowSolder
steps.does: Send the board through a reflow oven so the solder paste reflows and solders the components.

steps.name: AOIInspect
steps.does: Automated optical inspection checks every board for soldering and component placement defects.

steps.name: RouteRejectOrGood
steps.does: If AOI reports a failure, route the board to a reject lane; otherwise keep it in the good flow.

steps.name: OffCarrierToTote
steps.does: Remove good boards from the carrier into a tote.

output.quality: AOI checks every board; failed boards are diverted to a reject lane.
constraints: Guarded cells (safety fencing/containment around robot and oven areas)
Discrete, pallet-carrier throughput (board completes as one unit on the line)
assumptions: Target of one board every 45 seconds is fixed: takt = 45 s and line is sized to 80 finished boards/hour.
Pallet-carrier indexing between stations is synchronized to keep every station within 45 s per board.
The ‘carrier returns underneath’ means the empty carriers travel back to the start via a lower return path and do not interfere with forward flow.
The board remains attached/located on the carrier from paste application through AOI; removal happens only after AOI (good) and/or at the reject lane (bad).
Component feeders supply all ~20 components per board without changeover during the simulated run.

questions.question: What carrier hardware is used (e.g., dedicated PCB fixture on a pallet), and how exactly does the pallet conveyor carry and re-return under the board process?
questions.why: This determines the correct conveyor/fixture station interfaces and how the SCARA picks/places relative to the board.

questions.question: Does the reflow oven process time (including indexing/dwell and any cool-down needed before AOI) fit within the 45 s takt per board, or is it a batch/continuous oven with multiple boards in flight?
questions.why: The oven model affects station timing and whether AOI can run 1-board-per-takt.

questions.question: When a board fails AOI, how is it handled end-to-end: is it placed into a reject tote immediately, held on a separate reject carrier, or reworked?
questions.why: This changes the reject-lane station actions and the required pick/transfer operations after AOI.
